newsitem.title: GERMANY: German beet test points to good crop result.
newsitem.headline: German beet test points to good crop result.

text.p: The fourth German sugar beet test result, published on Monday, showed implied sugar yields progressed over the last two weeks and should support a better final crop figure, analysts said.
Sugar yield of 9.71 tonnes per hectare compared with 8.79 tonnes in the fourth test last year.
"It doesn't look unfavourable any more, sugar production could now exceed earlier forecasts if we get the right mixture of rainfall and sunshine during the beet campaign," an analyst said.

Sugar yields in the first two fortnightly tests this year were down, reflecting drought in the spring, but the third test was already more promising after rainy weather in August aided crop development.
Sugar content of 16.8 percent in today's test established a firm lead over last year's 15.8 percent.
Plant density of 85,100 per hectare compared with 76,900 last year was also a pointer to higher sugar yields.
Beet weight per hectare of 57.9 tonnes in the national test was up from 55.7 tonnes last year.
Analysts said this did not contradict the northern German industry result of 54.8 tonnes (63.5) published earlier today.
Soils in the South are generally more productive than sandy soils in the North, but production patterns in the North are more cohesive, allowing clearer clues to final results.
Sugar industry association WVZ, which collects the national data, maintained a 1996/97 sugar output forecast of 3.868 million tonnes, up 1.9 percent from 1995/96.
Growers are expected to start the beet harvest this week as stocks are empty.
